sampling_model.design: Population-level finite SCM identification from the full observed law with \(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y\) supplied to the decision problem; no experimental randomization is assumed.
sampling_model.units: The identification statements compare all finite SCMs inducing the same observed distribution; sampling enters only after identification.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention replaces the equations at \(X\) by the fixed assignment \(x\).
sampling_model.overlap: The novel input \(\Pi\) declares arbitrary positive or zero observed events. It is distinct from Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15's separability and parent conditions and from Theorem 18's treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); only denominators executed on a support branch must be certified positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not part of the kernel; a multinomial plug-in estimator is available after a guarded formula is returned.

Theorems 1--2 prove soundness of formula-returning algorithms for state-based causal effects under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints; the paper assumes a strictly positive observational distribution and does not claim completeness under those constraints.

body.tldr: The paper asks for a complete support-aware analogue of the ID algorithm, \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\), for finite latent DAGs with supplied observed alphabets, qualitative functional nodes, and declared positive or zero observed events. Its bounded partial-trace grammar must either refute the declarations, derive a guarded formula for \(P_x(y)\), or lift a local obstruction to two exact-support rational SCMs with the same observed law while preserving \(\Omega\) and the independent latent-source architecture of \(G\). An affirmative construction must additionally contain a trace-preserving embedding of the seven ordered Shpitser--Pearl ID cases on exactly the branch \(W=\varnothing\) with every observed cell positive; no support-specific or functional rule may fire there, successful compilation must reproduce the ordinary ID expression, and a failure payload must retain the actual failed subquery and its original-query provenance. The fully observed frontier and the supported-bow separation are available, but the general independent-source latent lift, rational equal-law witness theorem, converse formula reconstruction, finite grammar, certificate syntax, and explicit complexity bounds remain open. Accordingly, the classical-reduction proposition is deferred as a corollary of the missing embedding rather than asserted from the present construction handles.

project_justification.gap: Ordinary hedge completeness ignores declared structural-zero faces. Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under stated separability and parent conditions, and Theorem 18 assumes the treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither theorem identifies the arbitrary declared zero-and-positive support-literal regime introduced here. Chen--Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 are sound formula-returning algorithms for state-based effects under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints with a strictly positive observational law, not a complete formula-or-exact-support-countermodel procedure for valid intervention states on structural-zero faces. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove sound-and-complete gID under positivity of the observational law, not on arbitrary declared support faces, and do not supply exact-support rational paired witnesses. Tikka--Hyttinen--Karvanen Theorem 5 supplies a terminating sound CSI search, and Theorem 6 shows why contextwise answers do not give completeness.
project_justification.niche: Finite categorical latent SCMs with explicit observed alphabets admit combinatorial support certificates and canonical response coordinates, but existing tools do not coordinate them with query-specific hedge traces, exact witness lifting that preserves the latent-source architecture of \(G\), and auditable rational serialization.
project_justification.fill: A completed \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\) procedure must preserve \(\Omega\), exact support, functional-row provenance, and the latent-source architecture of \(G\) through recursion and certify every terminal outcome with a guarded formula, a contradiction, or a rational separating pair obeying explicit primitive and total bit bounds. On the nonfunctional full-support branch, the grammar must embed the seven ordered ordinary ID cases by a trace-preserving bisimulation, compile the same expression, and retain the failed subquery and original-query provenance at a hedge terminal. This invariant makes the classical reduction a derived sanity corollary once the concrete productions and compiler are constructed; it is not supplied by the current handles.

body.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl supply the recursive seven-case ID algorithm and its hedge completeness argument. The required classical branch here must preserve that recursion state-for-state, not merely agree with its final answer. In particular, a line-five failure must carry the actual failed call and \(\operatorname{FAIL}(G,G[S])\); its payload must certify the hedge at the failed query or subquery, Theorem 17 then certifies nonidentification there, and the conclusion transported to the original query has the corrected Theorem 19 scope: an appropriate subquery with outcome and intervention sets contained in those of the original query has a hedge. The present kernel additionally requires every nonclassical countermodel pair to preserve the declared exact support, supplied observed alphabets, qualitative functional rows, and the independent latent-source architecture of \(G\), with no shared root-mass requirement. Chen and Darwiche's Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under its stated separability and parent conditions, and Theorem 18 assumes the treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither handles arbitrary declared zero-and-positive support literals. Their constrained-identifiability work gives arithmetic-circuit invariant-cut tests, while their 2026 Theorems 1--2 give sound formula-returning algorithms for context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints under a strictly positive observational law; neither supplies the present complete exact-support rational-countermodel trichotomy. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove sound-and-complete gID under positivity of the observational law, not on arbitrary declared support faces. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen motivate provenance-preserving branching but do not provide the required completeness theorem. Fraser informs support consistency, Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe inform sourcewise cardinality bounds, and finite response-coordinate work informs polynomial encodings; none establishes the missing support-preserving independent-source rational lift.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The fully observed completion argument does not survive marginalization: equality of observed laws becomes a system of polynomial equalities in products of latent-source probabilities, so a local target-varying direction need not factor into independent sources, and a real separating fiber need not contain a rational point. In addition, the current trace and algorithm definitions are handles, not a production system, so even the classical full-support branch has no transition relation or compiler on which to prove the mandated seven-case bisimulation. These are open obligations, not assumptions.
body.honest_scope: The support oracle and fully observed completion frontier are established, and the supported-bow pattern has an explicit formula branch and exact rational separating pair. The general finite grammar, terminal-certificate syntax, support-preserving independent-source latent lift, rational equal-law witness theorem, converse guarded-formula reconstruction, kill-instance audit against concrete productions, and explicit functions \(H(L)\) and \(B_{\mathrm{rat}}(L)\) with search and checking bounds remain open. The classical-ID reduction is also deferred until concrete productions and a compiler satisfy the required trace-preserving embedding of all seven ordered cases; equality of final expressions alone is insufficient. A failure pair is scoped to its actual failed query or subquery, and only the corrected existential-subquery hedge conclusion is carried back to the original query. Generic real quantifier elimination, unrestricted latent flattening, and the fully observed special case do not resolve the latent headline.
